title: Stop the open-orders query from leaking statements

blocks.text: The support screen shows a customer's open orders. Its old query method handed the screen a live cursor, and the screen failed with `The object is already closed`. A quick rewrite fixed that, but after a day under load the database refuses new statements on long-lived connections, and once a request failed because the connection it was still using had been closed.

Write `openOrders(connection, customer)` in `src/main/java/practice/OrderQueries.java`. Read each row with the existing `read(rs)`. When the method returns or throws, nothing it opened is left open, and the connection it was lent is exactly as usable as before. Some old rows hold text such as `a box` in the `quantity` column; `read` throws `SQLException` on them, and that exception should reach the caller. About eight lines.

rows: 41 toner 85A 2 OPEN, 57 USB-C dock 1 SHIPPED, 63 paper A4 10 OPEN
`[OpenOrder[id=41, item=toner 85A, quantity=2], OpenOrder[id=63, item=paper A4, quantity=10]]`

cases.says: the customer's open orders come back oldest first, shipped ones and other customers' left out
a customer without open orders gets an empty list
the statement and result set the method opened are closed when it returns
the lent connection is still open and usable after the method returns
when a row can't be read, the SQLException reaches the caller and the statement is closed anyway

origin.section: A ResultSet Lives Only as Long as Its Statement

concepts: try-with-resources closes the result set and statement in reverse order, also when reading fails, and a method lent a connection leaves it open.
